code.note: Shell archive: read the text, do not execute it. Fortran/Sp/Drivers holds driver.f (TOMS451_PRB), and Drivers/res is the shipped reference output. Fortran/Sp/Src/src.f holds CHISQD (single precision REAL).

claim.location: Shipped reference output Fortran/Sp/Drivers/res, the first of the two lines for n = 10 under the column p = 0.5000 (the computed line, not the writeup line). Claim value: CHISQD(0.5, 10) = 9.341793.

reference.sha256: not computed; the value is quoted here and compared as a number

claim.metric: CHISQD(P, N) at P = 0.5, N = 10, the Chi-square quantile by Hill-type approximation, as printed by the driver (format f12.6).
claim.paper_value: Shipped driver table (writeup column, driver.f) gives 9.341794 for the same cell. Article text not read.

tolerance.basis: The reference prints 6 decimals (rounding 5e-7), and the writeup column differs from the computed column by 1e-6 in this cell. 1e-5 absolute covers printed rounding and single-precision libm rounding (about 1e-6 relative at this magnitude), and still catches a wrong algorithm. Fixed now, before any run; not to be loosened after a run. Note: other cells differ between computed and writeup columns by up to about 1e-2 (e.g. n=10, p=0.001: 29.589115 computed vs 39.589081 writeup); those are not used as claims.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: the driver evaluates 50 points.
cost.data_size: None: values are computed from P and N in the driver.
cost.data_licence: No data. Source is the public netlib TOMS collected-algorithms archive.

why: The driver evaluates CHISQD at fixed (P, N) and the shipped reference prints the computed values, so a rerun must run the Fortran routine to reproduce the value; it is not a closed form.
